text:
Montreal arrives at Winnipeg's door in better shape than its injury list suggests. The Canadiens won 4-1 at CHI two days ago and are 3-1-1 in their last five, all without Nick Suzuki, Ivan Demidov and Florian Xhekaj. Oliver Kapanen has taken Suzuki's spot beside Juraj Slafkovský and Cole Caufield. The Jets are winless in four (0-2-2) after a 3-2 overtime loss at DAL, missing Josh Morrissey, with Neal Pionk now on the first power-play unit and up to 25:50 a night from 22:56. Our chance numbers say the slump is real: they've had 45% of the expected goals, a measure of shot quality, in that stretch.

At five on five, MTL has taken 54% of the expected goals this season to WPG's 46%, though our model has tonight close, 3.15 to 3.06. Montreal also takes 5.5 penalties a game, which keeps feeding opponents' power plays. In net, projected starter Jakub Dobes is at -5.8 goals saved above expected (how many goals a goalie stops compared with an average one facing the same shots) in five games, after +17.3 last season. Stuart Skinner, projected for the Jets, is at +5.1 this year and +6.0 last.

Kyle Connor is our top scoring pick at 45% to score, with Caufield at 39% for Montreal. Arpon Basu of The Athletic posted that "85 percent or so of Cole Caufield's goals you can see coming from a mile away." Our under-the-radar pick is Cole Perfetti, 55% for a point, above his season pace of 46%, because his line creates chances. He's a player to watch, not a lock.
